note: The Ministry of Health registry lists each establishment twice, once in French and once in Arabic under two post ids, and the two posts are paired into one bilingual record; `refs.msp_twin` names the second post, so either id resolves to the record. The two posts usually sit at consecutive ids. This is what the twin-post recovery in packages/sante/scripts/fetch.mjs decided: the pairs it merged into one record, and every nearby candidate it refused, with the reason. A near post id is not evidence on its own, so a candidate must also pass a consonant-skeleton name check, a gap of two needs stronger name evidence than a gap of one, and an ambiguous candidate is left alone rather than guessed at. Four pairs across three cities sit 4, 10, 14 and 1284 post ids apart, too far for adjacency to reach them at all; those carry `decided_by: "pair_table"`, are asserted by hand in packages/sante/scripts/twin-pair-table.mjs, and publish there what their evidence covers. `second_source` is that evidence LEVEL and the two levels are not the same claim: `both` means a source which is not the registry names the establishment in both scripts, so it states the pair itself, and `fr_only` means the second source confirms the FRENCH half, with the Arabic half carried by `translation` (the two titles are exact translations of each other) and by `only_candidate_left` (it is the one candidate remaining in its wilaya and type group). The cases that table was asked about and left alone are listed in `unpaired_candidates`, with what is missing. `half_record_candidates` is the national measurement the same ticket asked for, recomputed from the shipped data on every build: every Half-record crossed with every Half-record of the other language in its own wilaya and type, with the post gap between them, so a refresh that leaves a new far-apart pair behind shows up here rather than as two records nobody notices. A row is a candidate and nothing more. Regenerated by `npm run fetch` in packages/sante.

unpaired_candidates.why: Skikda city publishes an 'Etablissement hospitalier' and an 'Etablissement Public Hospitalier', and both carry the city name and nothing else, so neither is the one candidate left in its group. Separating them needs a source that says which Skikda hospital is the public establishment and which is not. OpenStreetMap has two hospital buildings in the city, way/253913494 'Nouvel Hopital Abderezzak Bouhara' with no Arabic name at all and way/253914659 'Hopital de Skikda' / 'مستشفى سكيكدة', which is a toponym carrying neither legal class. Checked 2026-10-22: no ministry page, Journal Officiel text, Wikidata item or OpenStreetMap element names either establishment by its class, so both halves stay separate records.

unpaired_candidates.establishment: Skikda, the establishment the registry does not call public

unpaired_candidates.establishment: Ouargla, the establishment the registry calls public
unpaired_candidates.why: Ouargla reads like Skikda, one 'Etablissement hospitalier' and one 'Etablissement Public Hospitalier' of the city, but with a second doubt on top of the first: checked 2026-10-22, only ONE general hospital of Ouargla city could be found in any source, way/303499771 'Hopital Mohamed Boudiaf' (and it carries no Arabic name). The other two hospitals found are a different legal class, the ophthalmology hospital way/304632975 and the mother-and-child EHS way/377113766. So it is not established that these four posts are two establishments at all: they may be one, entered under an older and a newer legal name, which would be a repeat-post merge of four posts rather than two pairs. Pairing them would decide that question by assumption.
